# Spline object gate

`cases.txt` is generated by `generate.py` from NVIDIA USD BRep SMLib at
`c9c5979f04cea8c38213004d4f04df0dcfb40d05`. The test-only driver calls
`SmBSplineCurve`, `SmBSplineSurface` and the `SmNurbsSrf` control-net services.
Cargo reads these recorded results and never builds or links C++.

The oracle uses x86-64 Linux, the defines in rust-brep's `oracle/CMakeLists.txt`,
`-O2 -fno-fast-math -ffp-contract=off` and system TBB. The driver borrows
allocated NURBS representations with the input knots intact. It does not use
the raw surface constructor whose V-array copy has the U-array size limit.
Catallax owns checked vectors instead of copying the C++ allocation protocol.

The gate covers these services:

| Unit | Operations |
| --- | --- |
| `SmBSplineCurve.cpp` | Degree, dimension, counts, natural interval, ends, rational flag, Greville values, knots, all three control-point forms, degeneracy, excessive multiplicity, piecewise C0, repeated end controls, evaluation through fourth derivatives, zero-tangent replacement and axis-aligned boxes |
| `SmBSplineSurface.cpp` | Degrees, counts, natural domain, rational and bilinear flags, Greville values, knots, all three control-point forms, spans, repeated end controls, partial-net values and untrimmed isoparametric curves |
| `SmNurbsSrf.cpp` | Net extrema, Euclidean net access, net degeneracy, partial-net corners, normal box, chord heights, turning angles and splitting in either direction |
| Supporting NURBS routines | Curve basis derivatives, rational basis derivatives, point evaluation, curve splitting and isoparametric extraction |

The gate has 1,075 cases: 955 curves and 120 surfaces. It compares 251,482
binary64 outputs; 251,470 are bit-identical and the maximum difference is 3 ULP.
Inputs include regular, tangent, touching, singular, near-singular and boundary
cases. Curves include two and three dimensions, rational and non-rational
storage, clamped and unclamped knots, multiple spans, repeated interior knots,
endpoint clamps, collapsed polygons and zero end tangents. Surfaces include
rectangular nets, unequal degrees, collapsed rows and closed net boundaries.
The tests also compare every candidate output bit with one, two and four workers.

The curve and surface methods preserve their different side-flag mappings.
Derivative evaluation preserves NLib's reciprocal multiplication, while the
control accessors use direct division. SMLib's one-derivative zero-tangent
recursion defaults its recursive call to `FALSE`; the port preserves that
behaviour, including its difference from a two-derivative call.

Integers, flags and statuses match exactly. Every binary64 value has a 4 ULP
limit, including turning angles computed with `libm`'s inverse cosine. The
comparator has no absolute-error allowance near zero.
Opposite signed zeros differ. These limits compare candidates with C++ and
are never a Catallax modelling tolerance or an acceptance proof.

The owned API accepts degrees 1 through 31 and curve derivative orders 0
through 4. Higher orders, malformed storage, non-finite parameters, zero
control weights and invalid indexes return `Fault::InvalidInput`. A zero
rational denominator or a non-finite evaluated point returns
`Fault::Degenerate`. These refusals are tested separately from the C++ gate:
the gate compares operations with defined finite C++ results, including
SMLib's error status at an unclamped active endpoint. Evaluator errors also
return `Fault::Degenerate`. A box refuses if a required point evaluation
fails. SMLib can ignore that error and box default output values; the port
does not reproduce that result. A separate test exercises this refusal with
a knot-span width of `5e-25`.

This unit does not implement analytic subclasses, topology, fitting, trimmed
isoparametric curves, or pseudo and polar boxes. It does not claim Gate A or
Gate B intersection completion. All values remain unproved candidates, and
no production proof or saved replay answer consumes this module.

To regenerate, build the pinned SMLib outside the repository. `SMLIB_ROOT`
names its `source/SMLib` directory and `SMLIB_LIB_DIR` names the built library
directory. `ORACLE` and `RAW_DIR` name an executable and evidence directory
outside the repository.

```sh
c++ -std=c++17 -O1 -ffp-contract=off -w -DNDEBUG -DNOMINMAX \
  -DSM_GRAPHICS_CALLBACKS=1 -D_GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI=1 \
  -I"$SMLIB_ROOT/inc" crates/catallax-trace/tests/fixtures/spline/oracle.cpp \
  -L"$SMLIB_LIB_DIR" -Wl,-rpath,"$SMLIB_LIB_DIR" -lSMLib -ltbb -ltbbmalloc -o "$ORACLE"
python3 crates/catallax-trace/tests/fixtures/spline/generate.py "$ORACLE" "$RAW_DIR"
cargo test -p catallax-trace
```

Each oracle request has a fresh process, a 1 GiB address-space limit, a 10 s
CPU limit and a 20 s timeout. Raw evidence retained privately. No Mac or
arm64 gate is claimed.
